news.title: Uefa poised to lift boycott threat after Fifa promises no World Cup sale repeat
news.lede: Uefa has received guarantees after ill-fated Infantino plan. European sides likely to go to under-20 Women’s World Cup. Uefa is poised to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. The Guardian understands European teams are likely to be cleared for participation in the upcoming Under-20 Women’s World Cup, along with subsequent tournaments, after Fifa provided the binding assurances that no equivalent of its president’s ill-fated scheme will be put on the table.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: Uefa set to drop Fifa tournament boycott threat
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been president of Fifa since February 2016. Uefa is set to drop its threat of boycotting Fifa competitions, having received assurances there will be no repeat of Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, BBC Sport has been told. The matter will be discussed at a meeting of Uefa's executive committee in Monaco on Thursday. Earlier this month, European football's governing body said that despite Infantino's plan being aborted following widespread condemnation, the conditions required to prevent a boycott had "not been met".

news.title: SQUAD LIST: World Cup-bound Filipinas return to Asian Games
news.lede: The Philippine Women’s National Football Team (Filipinas) will compete in the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, marking the squad’s second consecutive appearance in Asia’s grandest multi-sport event following their quarterfinal finish in the 19th edition, played three years ago in Hangzhou, China. The campaign comes six months after the Filipinas secured their second consecutive FIFA Women’s World Cup appearance, defeating Uzbekistan in the playoff match of the 2026 AFC Women’s Asian Cup last March. The Filipinas have been drawn in Group G alongside three-time gold medalist China, Uzbekistan, and Hong Kong. The Philippines last faced China in the 2018 AFC Women’s Asian Cup in Amman, Jordan, falling 0-3, while they recently met Hong Kong in July 2025 during the 2026 AFC Women’s Asian Cup Qualifiers in Cambodia, winning 1-0.
